events.label: birth
events.text: Born Mary Carter in London.

evidence.quote: Raine was born Mary Carter in London on 17 February 1877

events.text: Became a probationary teacher in London, aged 14.

evidence.quote: After finishing school at 14 , she became a probationary teacher in London

events.text: Found work as a singer at Drury Lane and Adelphi Theatre, aged 17.

evidence.quote: at age 17 found work as a singer , including at Drury Lane and the Adelphi Theatre

events.text: Sailed with sister Daisy to Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia.

evidence.quote: In 1900 , at the age of 23 , Carter sailed with her sister Daisy to Moreton Bay in Queensland , Australia

events.text: Moved with sister Daisy to Sydney.

evidence.quote: In 1901 the two sisters moved to Sydney

events.text: Arrived in Nyngan to manage a hotel.

evidence.quote: but arrived there in 1902 to find that the hotel had no guests

events.text: Disembarked at Fremantle after abandoning return voyage.

evidence.quote: they abandoned the voyage , disembarking at Fremantle in 1904

events.text: Married William Morris Thomas.

evidence.quote: On 5 May 1905 , she married William Morris Thomas

events.text: Took the name Mary Thomas on marriage.

evidence.quote: On 5 May 1905 , she married William Morris Thomas , becoming Mary Thomas

events.text: Returned to Perth and moved into a house she had bought.

evidence.quote: in 1911 Mary returned to Perth , moving into a house that she had bought before the marriage

events.text: Bought the Bon Ton Cafe on William Street, her first business.

evidence.quote: In 1915 she bought her first business , the Bon Ton Cafe on William Street

events.text: Established Metropolitan Properties Ltd to manage her real estate.

evidence.quote: In 1924 , Thomas established Metropolitan Properties Ltd , with a capital value of £100,000

events.text: Bought Gordons Hotel for £40,000, half of it borrowed.

evidence.quote: That same year she bought the Gordons Hotel for £40,000

events.label: liquor licence
events.text: Obtained her first liquor licence.

evidence.quote: That same year she bought the Gordons Hotel for £40,000 , half of which she had borrowed , and obtained her first liquor licence

events.text: Major refurbishment and expansion of Gordons Hotel, about £27,000.

evidence.quote: In 1927 she undertook a major refurbishment and expansion of the hotel

events.text: Gordons Hotel reopened as the Wentworth Hotel.

evidence.quote: and in 1928 re-opened it as the Wentworth Hotel

events.text: Took over the lease of a hotel in Bullsbrook.

evidence.quote: In 1940 Thomas took over the lease of the newly refurbished hotel in Bullsbrook

events.text: Renamed the Bullsbrook hotel the Chequers Hotel.

evidence.quote: In 1940 Thomas took over the lease of the newly refurbished hotel in Bullsbrook , some from Perth , and renamed it the Chequers Hotel

events.text: Surrendered the Bullsbrook hotel lease after two years.

evidence.quote: she surrendered the lease after two years

events.text: US Navy requisitioned Wentworth; most hotels ceded to US forces.

evidence.quote: In 1942 , the fighting in World War II was getting closer to Australia

events.label: army ban
events.text: Australian Army banned its soldiers from the Wentworth Hotel.

evidence.quote: in 1943 the Australian Army banned its soldiers from the Wentworth

events.label: ban lifted
events.text: Army ban on the Wentworth lifted after Thomas wrote to PM Curtin.

evidence.quote: The ban was lifted a week later , after Thomas wrote to Prime Minister John Curtin

events.text: Married Arnold Yeldham (Joe) Raine.

evidence.quote: On 3 December 1943 , Mary Thomas married Arnold Yeldham

events.text: Took the name Mary Raine on marriage.

evidence.quote: On 3 December 1943 , Mary Thomas married Arnold Yeldham ( known as Joe ) Raine , thus becoming Mary Raine

events.text: US requisition of the hotels ended with the war.

evidence.quote: This arrangement lasted until the end of the war in 1945

events.text: Made a new will and deed of trust donating Joe's estate to UWA.

evidence.quote: In 1957 Raine made a new will

events.text: Husband Joe Raine died of a cerebral haemorrhage.

evidence.quote: On 11 February 1957 he suffered a cerebral haemorrhage and died

events.label: death
events.text: Died; buried alongside Joe at Karrakatta Cemetery.

evidence.quote: She died on 3 February 1960
